messages:
ravi: Quick heads-up — ran a run comparing mixed-precision kernels + different calibration sets on decoder-24 (A100). saw a weird 95th latency bump when we used per-channel calibration with the long-tail dialog samples.
sofia: curious — bump on which metric? p50/p95/p99?
matt: p50 looks fine, p95 spiked ~30% for workloads with lots of short-turn chat (seq <= 64) but also a handful of very long convo traces.
anika: do you have the perf logs? could be batching heuristics switching kernel mid-flight (batchlineage) when long sequences join a batch.
ravi: pasted output from profiler below — boiled down to kernel selection flips + KV warmup interplay
``` 
[profile] model=decoder-24 device=A100
batch=8 seq=32 kernel=int8_gemm latency=4.2ms tail95=12.8ms
batch=4 seq=512 kernel=fp8_gemm latency=18.3ms tail95=72.1ms
batch=8 seq=32 kernel=fp8_gemm latency=4.7ms tail95=85.9ms  # kernel flip -> big tail
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.12 -> 0.67 after warmup for same session
```
sofia: that 85.9ms tail is suspicious — same batch size but kernel changed. what's the kernel selection policy right now? threshold on seq*batch? or cost-model?
matt: we route by estimated tokens-per-request * hardware_score + fallback margin. but we do a cheap heuristic for mixed-precision: prefer int8 if seq*batch < 1024 else fp8. maybe that threshold is too coarse.
anika: and KV cache warmup can change seq distribution during a session — first few generations are longer (more context) then they shorten, so batchlineage mixes seq lengths and triggers kernel swap.
dave: also remember per-channel calibration shifts dynamic ranges on some attention heads -> some ops become slower on the int8 path (more dequant ops or slower matmuls) if calibration produced uneven scales.
ravi: exactly — when we used the calibration set with raw long-tail transcripts (many tokens per example) the per-channel scales were dominated by a few outliers, forcing bigger dynamic ranges on multiple channels. int8 kernels then added extra quant-dequant ops to preserve accuracy -> throughput drop.
sofia: did you try per-tensor calibration for the same set?
ravi: yes — per-tensor gave more conservative scales, int8 stayed fast but quality dropped slightly on rare tokens. per-channel preserved quality but hurt perf on mixed-batch workloads.
anika: can we clip outliers in cal set? like trim top 0.1% token magnitudes before computing scale?
matt: we tried percentile clipping but only globally. maybe we need per-layer outlier trimming + two-pass sampling (first pass to detect outliers per-channel, second to compute scale without them).
dave: proposal: two experiments
- EXP-A: per-tensor calib + percentile clip 99.9 + exclude docs > 100k tokens
- EXP-B: per-channel calib + layer-level outlier trim (trim top 0.05 per-layer) + pairing with kernel threshold adjustment (raise int8 threshold to 2048)
both run on the same request trace replay and measure p50/p95/p99 + accuracy on our eval set.
sofia: 👍 also add a batchlineage metric: how often batches contain mixed kernel affinities causing mid-batch kernel swaps.
ciara: @deploy-bot can you schedule replay jobs for EXP-A and EXP-B on staging GPUs? tag: eng-ml
deploy-bot: Scheduled: replay-1713456790-expA -> queued on staging-a (ETA 45m), replay-1713456790-expB -> queued on staging-b (ETA 50m)
sofia: another thought — KV warmup warms cache non-uniformly. If prefix caching yields different rare-key frequency, calibration set should include a mix of warm/cold sessions. our current cal set is mostly warm sessions pulled from high-traffic customers.
ravi: yep — biased cal set -> scales tuned to cached paths. that made long-tail cold sessions worse. we need a stratified cal set: cold-short, cold-long, warm-short, warm-long.
anika: actionable items
- assemble stratified calibration corpus (ravi, sofia)
- run EXP-A/B replays and collect p50/p95/p99 + per-route kernel-choice histogram (matt)
- add batchlineage counters and KV-warmup flagging to profiler (dave)
- evaluate quality delta on eval prompts focusing on tail tokens (anika)
ravi: timeline? can we get initial numbers by EOD tomorrow?
matt: replay jobs will finish in ~1h each; analysis another 2-3h. EOD is tight but possible.
sofia: I'll start curating the stratified cal corpus now. will push a spec: include at least 5000 short-cold sessions and 500 long-cold sessions, plus warm mixes.
dave: if we see per-channel still bad after trimming, fallback is to prefer per-tensor for mixed-batch routes and per-channel for dedicated low-variance routes.
anika: agreed. also log a ticket to update our kernel selection policy to use expected op-cost from calibration profile rather than coarse seq*batch threshold.
sofia: noted. I'll add the ticket and link here once created.
ravi: nice — thanks everyone. keeping an eye on the replays.
sofia: :rocket: good set of experiments. ping if anything blocks.
